events.title: Joan of Arc reaches besieged Orléans
events.shortBlurb: The young peasant maid entered the beleaguered city and turned the tide of the Hundred Years' War…
body: On the evening of 29 April 1429 Joan of Arc, a peasant girl of about seventeen from Domrémy in Lorraine, rode into Orléans with a relieving force; the city had been besieged by the English since October, and its fall would have opened all France south of the Loire. She went, she said, at God's command, guided by the voices of Michael the Archangel, Catherine of Alexandria, and Margaret.

Within days the French carried the English bastions, and on 8 May the besiegers struck their camp and withdrew. The deliverance of Orléans turned the tide of the Hundred Years' War; that July the dauphin was crowned at Reims as Charles VII, Joan standing beside the altar with her banner.

Taken by the Burgundians at Compiègne in May 1430 and sold to the English, she was condemned by an ecclesiastical court at Rouen and burned on 30 May 1431. That judgment was annulled in 1456; Benedict XV canonized her on 16 May 1920, and she is honored as a patroness of France.
